question: Can the design of agentic systems be automated by having a meta agent program new agents in code and search over them?
hypothesis: Searching in code space with a meta agent and a growing archive finds agents that beat hand-designed ones and transfer across domains and models.
contributions: Define Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ADAS) with three components: search space, search algorithm, evaluation function.
Propose Meta Agent Search, a meta agent programming new agents in code from an archive of earlier ones.
Show discovered agents beat state-of-the-art hand-designed agents on ARC, DROP, MGSM, MMLU, GPQA and transfer across domains and models.

method.summary: A meta agent (GPT-4o) writes a Python forward() function defining a new agent given an archive of prior agents and their validation scores; the agent gets two self-reflection passes, is evaluated on validation data (up to 5 debug retries on runtime errors), and is added to the archive. Runs are 25 iterations (ARC) or 30 (other domains); discovered agents are run on gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 and compared with seven hand-designed agents and OPRO prompt optimisation.
method.task: Search for agentic system code that maximises validation accuracy or F1 on a target domain

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant. Make sure to return in a WELL-FORMED JSON object.

You are an expert machine learning researcher testing various agentic systems. Your objective is to design building blocks such as prompts and workflows within these systems to solve complex tasks. Your aim is to design an optimal agent performing well on [Brief Description of the Domain]. ... # Your task You are deeply familiar with prompting techniques and the agent works from the literature. Your goal is to maximize the specified performance metrics by proposing interestingly new agents. Observe the discovered agents carefully and think about what insights, lessons, or stepping stones can be learned from them. Be creative when thinking about the next interesting agent to try. You are encouraged to draw inspiration from related agent papers or academic papers from other research areas. Use the knowledge from the archive and inspiration from academic literature to propose the next interesting agentic system design. THINK OUTSIDE THE BOX.

Error during evaluation: [Runtime errors] Carefully consider where you went wrong in your latest implementation. Using insights from previous attempts, try to debug the current code to implement the same thought. Repeat your previous thought in "thought", and put your thinking for debugging in "debug thought".

limits: Only single-step QA tasks evaluated; multi-step environment interaction left to future work (Sec 6).
Single objective (performance); cost, latency and robustness not optimised.
Search algorithm is naive (archive prompting only); evaluation function is expensive and ignores logs (Sec 6, App J).
Search and test subsets are small (800 test questions, 60 on ARC); several gains on MMLU and GPQA are within the CIs; one search run per domain, search seeds not reported.
Meta agent and evaluated models are 2024 models (GPT-4o, GPT-3.5); agent gains may shrink as base models improve, as the authors themselves note for knowledge-limited domains.
Safety: generated code can be destructive; mitigated by containers and manual inspection, not formally guaranteed.
Claude-Haiku transfer shows weak or no advantage on ARC.

terms.definition: Automated Design of Agentic Systems involves using a search algorithm to discover agentic systems across a search space that optimize an evaluation function.
Iteratively have a meta agent program new agents in code from an ever-growing archive of previous discoveries.
